newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court rejects complaint by couriers against La Poste.
newsitem.headline: Court rejects complaint by couriers against La Poste.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance (CFI) rejected on Wednesday pleas from French based international couriers to overturn a European Commission decision dismissing complaints against France's La Poste.

SFEI, DHL, Service CRIE and May Courier asked the CFI to force the Commission to find the relationship between La Poste, France's postal service, and its subsidiary Societe francaise de messageries internationales (SFMI), anti-competitive.

The Commission rejected these complaints in a letter from Commissioner Karel Van Miert who told the applicants the pursuit of such a claim would only satisfy the individual interests of the complainants, but would serve no Community interest.

The court found the Commission's decision not to pursue the complaint was properly based on a finding of insufficient Community interest. At the time the decision was made, the Commission said the practices alleged as violations had stopped, and the complainants offered no proof to the contrary.
The CFI said the Commission can legitimately decide not to pursue a complaint if the practices in question have ceased, especially if the Commission played a part in putting a stop to the practices.
"Concurrence - Recours en annulation - Rejet d'une plainte - Interet communautaire"
Commission des Communautes europeennes, partie defenderesse
ayant pour objet l'annulation de la decision SG (94) D/19144 de la Commission, du 30 decembre 1994, rejetant la plainte du Syndicat francais de l'express international du 21 decembre 1990
2. Les requerants sont condamnes aux depens.
